figure: Table 2-1 — Decode bandwidth and prefill FLOPs
issue: The table starts at the very foot of the page: caption, header row and only two data rows ('Model params 70B', 'Model weight bytes (FP16) 140 GB') fit before the page break, with the remainder presumably continuing on printed p.21. A table that begins with two visible rows and then breaks across a page is hard to read and, absent a continuation cue, invites the reader to mis-read the first two rows as the whole table.
evidence: Rendered page: caption 'Table 2-1 — Decode bandwidth and prefill FLOPs (worked example, not reference)' sits at roughly two-thirds down the page, followed by the header and two rows; the page ends immediately after the second row. The two visible rows are arithmetically consistent with the prose ('a 70B-class dense model in FP16'; 70e9 x 2 B = 140 GB).
acceptance_test: Keep Table 2-1 together on one page (push it to printed p.21) or, if it must break, add a 'Table 2-1 (continued)' header on the following page. Acceptance: no table in the book begins with fewer than three rows before a page break, and any continued table carries a continuation cue.

issue: The drawn roofline is inconsistent with the stated H100 bandwidth. At arithmetic intensity 1 FLOP/byte, the black roofline intersects the left axis at about 1e12 FLOP/s, but 3.35 TB/s implies 3.35e12 FLOP/s. The drawn line therefore has a log-log slope of about 1.21 instead of 1, even though the caption and ridge label claim a 3.35 TB/s roofline with ridge at ~295 FLOP/byte.
evidence: Figure 2.2 caption: 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 → ridge at 295 FLOP/byte'. Roofline: attainable = min(989e12, AI × 3.35e12). At AI = 1, attainable = 3.35e12 FLOP/s, not 1e12. The drawn black line starts at approximately (1, 1e12) and reaches (295, 989e12), which is not the stated bandwidth slope.
acceptance_test: Recompute and redraw the memory-bound segment through (1, 3.35e12) and (295, 989e12); verify the log-log slope is 1 and the intercept matches 3.35 TB/s. Confirm the decode marker at ~1 FLOP/byte sits below the corrected roof, not below a too-low roof.

figure: Figure 2.2 (Prefill and decode: two regimes split by the roofline ridge)
issue: The caption's italic 'Regime' clause states the canonical prefill point is '~0.2K FLOP/byte' and on the same line calls it 'well to the right of the ~295 ridge'. 0.2K = 200 FLOP/byte, which is LEFT of the 295 ridge, so the clause is internally self-contradictory and contradicts the plotted prefill marker on the same page.
evidence: The drawn prefill triangle sits at x ≈ 1e4 on the log x-axis (far right of the red 295 ridge line). Independent rederivation from the book's own canonical inputs: prefill FLOPs ≈ 2·P·N = 2·70e9·9200 ≈ 1.29e15; bytes ≈ weights streamed once = 2·70e9 = 1.4e11; arithmetic intensity = 1.29e15 / 1.4e11 ≈ 9.2e3 = 9.2K FLOP/byte (≈ the 9,200-token prompt length, because in the parallel prefill pass each weight byte is reused once per prompt token). 9.2K is well right of 295 and matches the plotted marker. The printed '0.2K' is off by ~46× and cannot simultaneously be 'well to the right of the ~295 ridge'. The figure is correct; the caption number is the defect.
acceptance_test: Replace '~0.2K FLOP/byte' with '~9.2K FLOP/byte' (or '~9K'). After the edit, confirm (a) the value exceeds 295 so 'well to the right of the ~295 ridge' is true, (b) it is consistent with the plotted marker near 1e4, and (c) it equals N under the 2·P·N / (2·P) = N derivation used elsewhere in the book.

figure: Figure 2.2 (Prefill and decode: two regimes split by the roofline ridge)
issue: The same caption's 'Capacity' clause cites the single-H100 theoretical peak as '0.980 PFLOPS', but the figure's own flat roof is labeled '989 TFLOPS' (= 0.989 PFLOPS) and the in-repo datasheet / house canonical dense value is 989 TFLOPS. Same-page figure and caption disagree on the canonical hardware number.
evidence: 989 TFLOPS = 0.989 PFLOPS ≠ 0.980 PFLOPS. The '1.19 PFLOPS demand > peak' conclusion is numerically unaffected (1.19 > 0.98 either way), but a careful reader comparing the roof label to the caption on the same page sees 989 vs 980. The 1.19 PFLOPS demand itself is consistent (1.29e15 prefill FLOPs / 1.08 s prefill budget ≈ 1.19e15), so only the peak figure is misstated.
acceptance_test: Replace '0.980 PFLOPS' with '0.989 PFLOPS' (989 TFLOPS) to match the figure's roof label and the datasheet; grep the page (and any cross-referencing text) to confirm no residual '980'/'0.980' remains for the dense H100 peak.

figure: FIG 2.2 — Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge
issue: The caption's opening phrase — 'Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge' — contradicts the figure's own title and content. The in-figure title reads 'Prefill and decode: two regimes split by the roofline ridge', and the two markers sit on opposite sides of the ridge (decode at AI ≈ 1 FLOP/byte, left of the ridge; prefill at AI ≈ 5,000 FLOP/byte, right of it). 'On the ridge' reads as 'both regimes sit at the ridge', which is the opposite of the point the figure exists to make.
evidence: Caption: 'FIGURE 2.2: Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge. Low-batch decode (streaming weights per token) lands at ~1 FLOP/byte — the memory-bound side; long-prompt prefill lands at high intensity — the compute-bound side.' In-figure title: 'Prefill and decode: two regimes split by the roofline ridge'. Red dashed ridge line at ~295 FLOP/byte; decode marker on the '1' tick; prefill marker between the 1000 and 10000 ticks.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption's first sentence to 'Prefill and decode on either side of the roofline ridge' (or '... split by the roofline ridge'). Acceptance: the caption no longer asserts that either regime lies at the ridge, and the caption's first clause agrees with the in-figure title.

issue: The two markers are encoded inconsistently against the y-axis, and the prefill marker is drawn exactly on the compute ceiling. The prefill triangle straddles the 1e+15 gridline (989 TFLOPS = the H100 BF16 dense peak), i.e. at 100% of peak, while the decode circle sits roughly 3.5x below the bandwidth ceiling (≈1.2e12 FLOPS at AI = 1, where the ceiling is 3.35e12). The figure's own annotation — 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)' — is contradicted by a marker drawn on the roof. A reader can legitimately infer 'prefill runs at 989 TFLOPS', which is not a claim the book can support.
evidence: Rendered page: prefill triangle centred on the 1e+15 line at x ≈ 5,000 FLOP/byte; the black diagonal roofline reaches (ridge ≈ 295 FLOP/byte, 1e15 FLOPS); the decode circle sits at (1 FLOP/byte, ≈1.2e12 FLOPS) while the diagonal at AI = 1 is at 3.35e12 FLOPS. In-figure annotation: 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)'. Independent recomputation of the canonical decode intensity: 2 x 70e9 FLOPs/token ÷ 140e9 B/token = 1.0 FLOP/byte, consistent with the marker; canonical prefill intensity ≈ (2 x 70e9 x 9200) ÷ ~1.6e11 B ≈ 8-9 kFLOP/byte, i.e. the marker at ~5 kFLOP/byte is roughly a factor of two below the canonical point.
acceptance_test: Choose one of: (a) move the prefill marker below the 1e+15 line (e.g. to ~1e14) so that no marker touches a ceiling; (b) add an explicit note adjacent to the markers, 'regime only — vertical position is not an achieved-throughput claim'; or (c) if the markers are intended to be the canonical operating points, place prefill at ≈9 kFLOP/byte and decode at 1 FLOP/byte and say so in the caption. Acceptance: after re-render, no marker lies on either ceiling line, or the caption states the markers' meaning unambiguously.

issue: The annotation 'markers = regime, not measured MFU' uses MFU (model FLOPs utilization — a ratio of achieved to peak FLOPs) to describe a y-axis labelled 'attainable performance (FLOPS)' (an absolute rate). The two are not interchangeable, and the reader is given no way to relate the annotation to the axis it annotates.
evidence: In-figure annotation: 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)'; y-axis label: 'attainable performance (FLOPS)'; the 989 TFLOPS peak is drawn as a ceiling line.
acceptance_test: Replace 'not measured MFU' with 'not measured throughput' (or 'not an achieved-FLOPS claim'), or state the relationship explicitly ('markers indicate regime, not achieved FLOPS; MFU is not implied'). Acceptance: the annotation uses only terms defined in the book and is dimensionally consistent with the axis it annotates.

issue: Two legibility collisions inside the plot area. (i) The hardware annotation 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 → ridge at 295 FLOP/byte' is printed directly over the diagonal hatch fill of the memory-bound region, reducing contrast for a line that carries the figure's key constants. (ii) The red 'decode' wordmark sits on the lower-left end of the black roofline stroke, so label and line share pixels.
evidence: Rendered page: the annotation line sits at the bottom-left of the plot area, inside the diagonally hatched region; the 'decode' wordmark is positioned at the origin of the black diagonal line, immediately above the red circle marker.
acceptance_test: Give the hardware annotation an opaque background plate (or move it below the x-axis, or into the caption), and nudge the 'decode' label clear of the roofline stroke. Acceptance: at 150 dpi, both texts read with no hatch or line pixels inside the glyphs.

figure: Figure 3.1 — panel A, 'Continuous diffusion (schematic state values)'
issue: Panel A encodes continuous state with a bar chart, which is the conventional glyph for a categorical probability distribution — and the figure's entire purpose is to contrast a continuous lane with a categorical lane (panel B uses token boxes). Panel B carries an explicit note ('M = MASK; text states are illustrative token IDs, not generated results') but panel A carries no equivalent note, so the bars can be read as token probabilities. That is precisely the category error the surrounding prose warns against ('Text requires a discrete construction because token IDs are categories, not continuous pixel values'), and it undercuts the continuous-vs-discrete contrast the figure exists to establish.
evidence: PDF 51 / printed 31, panel A; prose immediately below the caption: 'Text requires a discrete construction because token IDs are categories, not continuous pixel values.'
acceptance_test: Add a panel-A note stating what the bars are (e.g. 'bars are schematic magnitudes of continuous state coordinates, not token probabilities'), or replace the bar chart with a continuous-valued glyph (smooth curve, coordinate scatter) so the continuous lane is not encoded with a distribution glyph. Acceptance: no reader can read panel A as a categorical distribution.

issue: The three panels of the continuous lane are drawn with essentially the same bar pattern, so the 'noise prior' panel is not visually distinguishable from the 'clean diffusion data' panel. The forward direction (data -> partly corrupted -> noise) is therefore not readable from the drawing; the reader must rely on the arrow labels and the caption to know which end is noise. As rendered, the figure does not show the corruption progression it describes.
evidence: PDF 51 / printed 31, panel A: the bar patterns in 'clean diffusion data', 'partly corrupted' and 'noise prior' are visually near-identical at print size; no equal-magnitude or noise-texture treatment distinguishes the prior.
acceptance_test: Make the noise-prior panel visually distinct (equal-magnitude bars, or a noise texture) and make 'partly corrupted' visibly intermediate between data and noise. Acceptance: the reader can identify the forward direction and the endpoint of the forward process from the drawing alone, without reading the caption.

figure: Figure 3.2 — panels B and C (source box vs. canvas relationship)
issue: Panels B and C place a box labelled 'fixed prompt' / 'causal prefix' immediately before a canvas whose leading cells are unresolved ('?'), while panel A places 'fixed prefix' before a canvas whose first cell is already resolved ('A'). Under the convention panel A establishes (the canvas is the growing prefix), panels B and C contradict their own labels: a fixed prompt and a causal prefix cannot be drawn as unresolved '?' cells. Under the alternative convention (the canvas excludes the prefix), panel A's note 'Accepted IDs extend the prefix' becomes false. The figure never states which convention holds, so the reader cannot determine, for any panel, which cells are already committed.
evidence: PDF 54 / printed 34: panel A 'fixed prefix' -> [A][-][-][-]; panel B 'fixed prompt' -> [?][?][?][?]; panel C 'causal prefix' -> [?][?][-][-]. Panel B note: 'accepted IDs stay fixed'; panel C note: 'Refine the active block; finalize/cache its state before advancing.'
acceptance_test: Add one explicit convention line (in the figure or its caption) stating whether the source box's tokens are drawn inside the canvas, then make all three panels obey it: if the canvas includes the prefix, panels B and C must show the prompt/prefix cells as fixed (solid, lettered) rather than '?'; if it does not, panel A's 'Accepted IDs extend the prefix' note must be reworded. Acceptance: for each panel the reader can state which cells are committed, which are unresolved, and which are inactive future.

figure: Figure 3.2 — 'solid brackets' convention (panel A note and caption)
issue: Both the in-figure note ('Solid brackets mark finalized prefix state, not just accepted IDs') and the caption ('Solid brackets identify finalized prefix state') rely on a solid-vs-non-solid border convention, but the inactive-future '-' cells are drawn with the same solid outline as accepted-ID cells. The legend defines a border convention only for '?' (hatched). As drawn, the note's claim cannot be verified from the figure, and a reader could reasonably take the trailing '-' cell as finalized prefix state — the exact confusion the note was written to prevent.
evidence: PDF 54 / printed 34, panel A third state [A][B][C][-]: the '-' cell carries the same solid blue outline as the 'A', 'B', 'C' cells. Legend: 'Letters = accepted IDs; hatched ? = unresolved; - = inactive future.'
acceptance_test: Give '-' cells a distinct treatment (dashed or ghost outline, or lighter fill) and state it in the legend, so finalized prefix state is visually separable from inactive future in every panel; or delete the 'solid brackets' sentences and rely on the legend alone. Acceptance: in every panel, finalized state, unresolved state, and inactive future are separable by border/fill alone, without reading the notes.

figure: Figure 3.2 — panel B trace vs caption claim
issue: The caption says the full-canvas masked sampler 'accepts positions out of order', but the drawn trace accepts positions strictly left to right: [?][?][?][?] -> [A][B][C][?] -> [A][B][C][D]. The one property that distinguishes full-canvas sampling from the autoregressive panel in panel A — out-of-order acceptance — is not shown, so the figure cannot support the caption's claim and a reader comparing panels A and B sees only a difference in re-evaluation, not in acceptance order.
evidence: PDF 54 / printed 34, panel B trace vs caption sentence 'a full-canvas masked sampler that accepts positions out of order while recomputing bidirectional states'.
acceptance_test: Either change the panel B trace so at least one step accepts a non-leftmost position (e.g. [?][?][?][?] -> [A][?][C][?] -> [A][B][C][D]), or reword the caption to describe what is drawn ('recomputes the full canvas at every step; the accepted set is shown growing'). Acceptance: the caption's distinguishing clause is visible in the drawing.

issue: The caption states 'Loops represent repeated evaluations, not fixed steps or proportional time', but the drawing contains no loop. It contains a bracket labelled 'repeat evaluations' under the last transition of panels B and C. The caption names a graphical element that does not exist.
evidence: PDF 54 / printed 34: the only repetition marker is an orange bracket labelled 'repeat evaluations'.
acceptance_test: Either draw a return arrow and keep the caption's word 'Loops', or change the caption to 'The bracket marks repeated evaluations'. Acceptance: every graphical noun used in the caption corresponds to a drawn element.

issue: The caption reads 'schematic widths do not step counts', which is missing a verb and is not grammatical. The note inside the figure has the correct wording ('Schematic: stage widths do not encode step counts'), so the caption is a degraded copy of the figure's own text.
evidence: PDF 63 / printed 43: caption 'schematic widths do not step counts' vs in-figure note 'Schematic: stage widths do not encode step counts.'
acceptance_test: Caption reads 'schematic widths do not encode step counts'.

figure: Figure 3.3 — 'Denoising schedule progresses / Not two experts within one forward' label
issue: The two-line label sits between the two dashed checkpoint-to-stage arrows and reads as annotating only the right-hand arrow (the low-noise checkpoint), which is where the eye lands last. The statement is a property of the pair of checkpoints, not of the low-noise branch, and the caption's 'only the selected expert runs in a branch evaluation' is the point the figure is trying to make.
evidence: PDF 63 / printed 43: the label is centered between the two dashed arrows, closer to the right arrow's shaft.
acceptance_test: Move the label to a centered line spanning both arrows, or into the caption, so it reads as a property of the checkpoint pair. Acceptance: the label is not visually attached to a single arrow.
